A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSI research on steering Llama-2 toward AI coordination. All 41 pages of v1 and 14 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison despite the changed title and substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original attention-head sweeps, intervention comparisons and scored model responses. Only its SFT comparison score is explicitly borrowed from prior work.

after.justification: V2 reports original intervention results, SFT experiments, human validation of the judge and steering-direction analyses.

M1.justification: HSI retains contrastive mean-difference directions, additive attention-head interventions, binary-choice probing to select heads and subsequent open-ended generation. The added diagnostic experiments and revised completion-preparation description do not introduce a new HSI component.

E1.justification: V2 adds dedicated Anthropic evaluations for coordination with itself and other model versions, with 75 examples each (Table 4). This is a limited expansion within the existing coordination domain: v1 Appendix A.2 already includes individual prompts concerning copies and older versions of the model.

E2.justification: SFT joins the binary-choice validation/test comparison in v2 Table 2; v1 Table 3 provided no SFT accuracy result. SFT was already represented in the open-ended comparison, and the unmodified baseline, CAA and ITI remain.

E3.justification: Open-ended evaluation changes from GPT-4 to GPT-4.5 and adds validation using 28 responses rated by three humans. V2 trains its own SFT baseline on 100 HSI-selected completions for six epochs instead of borrowing its score. Section 4.2 also replaces three contrastive completions per behavior with a manually created pair in the reported preparation procedure; this does not establish that retained sweeps were rerun. The primary 180/180/50 split remains equivalent.

E4.justification: V2 Table 1 adds individual-head versus combined-head ablations across three intervention strengths. New Section 5, Figure 4, Table 5 and Appendix B examine cosine alignment, intervention failures and opposing sample-specific/general directions. Judge validation is also added. The earlier head sweeps and CAA-versus-HSI example remain, while the per-prompt comparison plot is removed.

E5.justification: V2 adds human–judge correlation reporting and four-generation consistency checks for SFT selection and direction analysis. The original six-generation head sweeps remain; an increase in repetitions for those experiments is not established. Neither version supplies seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing binary-choice test accuracies remain unchanged, but newly reported SFT accuracy of 0.86 exceeds HSI's 0.82. V1's open-ended HSI/SFT scores of 4.75/3.66 are replaced by 3.65/2.85 for Other AIs under GPT-4.5 and revised SFT training, so these are not comparable performance declines. V2 adds self/version results, ablation and cosine findings, and human–judge correlation of 0.95. V1's per-prompt plot and 50-response scored appendix log are removed.

T1.justification: The attention decomposition, additive intervention and contrastive mean-difference formulation remain. Explicit last-token dimensions and the expanded residual-update equation clarify the existing formulation; no new theorem, proof or substantive formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The central claims about bypassing alignment through sparse head interventions and generalizing beyond binary-choice probing remain. V2 modestly extends the explicit contribution list to include limitations of the general intervention direction.

C2.justification: V1 already warns that averaging misaligned directions can undermine steering. V2 extends this interpretation by linking cosine alignment to reliability and explaining how an opposing direction can counteract the intended behavior. The existing ITI explanation and limitations concerning coherence, linear separability and manual head selection largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly provides a project code/data access statement and SFT implementation details: RMSProp, six epochs, a cosine scheduler and a selected learning rate of 10^-5 after searching 10^-4 to 10^-6. The hardware description changes from one to two GTX 3090 GPUs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bengio et al. on managing extreme AI risks and removes Koo et al. and the discussion of attention-head probing in music transformers. The main positioning relative to CAA and ITI is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, dataset description, head-identification account and results interpretation undergo substantial rewriting. The paper is retitled, multiple-choice terminology becomes binary-choice terminology, and the narrative is reorganized around separate SFT, test-evaluation and direction-limit sections.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different journal layout and adds an overview diagram incorporating v1 Table 1's crane example. Existing sweeps are reformatted, the HSI table gains individual-head columns, and the combined results table becomes separate binary-choice and open-ended tables. New correlation/cosine displays and an appendix case-study panel are added; the per-prompt score plot is removed.

improvement.justification: V1 reports no human validation of its GPT-4 judge and borrows its SFT score. V2 substantially strengthens the evidence through an independently trained SFT comparison, human validation of GPT-4.5 and analyses explaining head contributions and steering failures. These address important weaknesses in comparative evaluation and understanding of applicability. Removing the detailed response log reduces in-PDF auditability, but the new validation and diagnostic evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
